newsitem.title: GERMANY: No EU deal to delay Italy EMU entry - German source.
newsitem.headline: No EU deal to delay Italy EMU entry - German source.

text.p: The European Union (EU) has made no political agreements over delaying Italy's entry into the planned European Monetary Union, a German government source said.

EU bureaucrats may be discussing EMU scenarios, but neither politicians nor senior bureaucrats were involved in discussions of what countries may or may not participate in EMU in the first round in 1999, the source told Reuters.
The source was responding to a report in the Financial Times of a face-saving deal that would delay Italy's entry into EMU until 2000 or 2001.
A German Finance Ministry spokeswoman, also commenting on the report, told Reuters, "There are no such plans with German participation."
Several senior German central bankers have openly voiced fears that Italy's participation would weaken the future single currency, the euro.
But Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi said Italy was "solemnly commited" to joining EMU at the outset.
